The Vale Federation
The Vale Federation is a group of schools in Aylesbury. The schools in the Vale Federation are Booker Park primary special school and Stocklake Park secondary special school which has a dedicated special 6th Form catering for post 16 students.
The Vale Federation is made up of Booker Park and Stocklake Park Special Schools, and we are fortunate in enjoying some amazing facilities, from a hydrotherapy pool and sensory room, through to a rebound centre, and fantastic playground spaces. We look for all our young people to be successful learners, enabling them to achieve in a caring and supportive environment. Working together is at the heart of The Vale Federation and our relationship with parents, carers and all the many professionals is central to helping our young people succeed. Every member of staff at The Vale Federation is committed to serving the best interests of those attending our schools and we invite you to join us in our drive for excellence within our specialist sector.
Inspire – Enable – Achieve
The Vale Federation is a group of special schools in Aylesbury. This includes Booker Park School Primary and Stocklake Park Secondary School which has a dedicated 6th Form catering for post 16 students.
The Vale Federation website gives you an insight to our central team, central services and wonderful facilities available for both businesses and our local community to hire.
At the heart of our Federation is our commitment to enabling our young people to reach and achieve their full potential in a caring, considerate and supportive environment, working closely with parents and carers and the many professional specialist teams and therapists involved in their day to day development.
Everyone works to make this happen from ensuring the facilities are clean to raising funds for new resources, from supporting personal care to teaching a young person to communicate, from ensuring they get to school to sharing their day on their return – we all have a part to play. Together we work to provide the best that we possibly can to support all their unique learning needs.

Careers at The Vale Federation
Educational development is our key goal, there are so many supporting elements that assist in achieving that objective, delivered by a comprehensive team of people across so many functions. That’s what makes working for The Vale Federation so interesting and exciting – the variation of job roles to make this happen. We have a number of different roles across our departments from Teaching and Learning to Catering, Facilities and Estates, IT, HR, Paediatric Moving and Handling, Finance and Administration, all with career development opportunities across a growing organisation.

pageCache.pageTitle: February 2026 – Sensory Room Installation Reveal - The Vale Federation
pageCache.text:
February 2026 – Sensory Room Installation Reveal
We are pleased to announce that, upon our return from half-term last week, we unveiled the newly installed Sensory Room at Stocklake Park School.
We had the pleasure of welcoming Ben and his wonderful son Max – a Stocklake Park student, to the official reveal. Together Ben and Max’s step-mum Jennie, generously contributed £12,000 towards the renovations and equipment, raised through their wedding. Our school charity MASKS also contributed additional funds towards the installation through their fundraising efforts.
The new Sensory Room features padded walls with vibrating panels, iPad-controlled lighting, and a ceiling projector that displays interactive imagery onto the floor.
Our staff were delighted to explore the new space and are looking forward to spending time in the room with students. The Sensory Room now provides a calm, soothing, and engaging environment where students can retreat to whenever they need to.
We would like to say a big thank you to Ben and Jennie, Max’s parents, and to MASKS for their generosity and support.

Current Careers at The Vale Federation
The Vale Federation is an organisation which has a wide range of job roles, across many functions, all with the same purpose and goal of delivering the best possible outcomes for all our pupils. Educational development remains our key goal with many supporting elements to assist in achieving that objective, delivered by a comprehensive team of people across so many functions. The variation of roles is what makes working for The Vale Federation so interesting and exciting, with such a broad and diverse range of departments including; Teaching and Learning to Catering, Facilities and Estates, IT, Finance, Health and Safety, HR, Payroll, Administration and more, there are outstanding career development opportunities across an innovative organisation.
What Our Staff Say
Debbie, Teacher
Imagine getting up in the morning knowing that you will make a difference that day. Well, this is one of the benefits of working at Booker Park School. Being in a highly staffed class with a small number of pupils allows for strong relationships with the children and their families and this helps you to make the difference! Working as a team with the therapists, we plan and implement a multi-sensory curriculum that meets the individual needs of children. Yes, the day can be challenging. Understanding behaviours, organising lessons around staffing, and keeping up to date with paperwork. However, when you have a moment of reflection at the end of the day and you remember the child that made a verbal request for the first time, and the boy that finally completed an activity on his own, that is why you work at Booker Park school.
Annette, Payroll Manager
I have worked for the Federation since 2016. My main role is to process Payroll for over 300 staff, which at times, can have its challenges, but from day one I have received full training and support, with plenty more training opportunities available to me. What I like about having a challenge, is working through them to see the positive results and benefits at the end. Although I am office based, I make sure I have interaction with staff at all levels. Working as part of a solid, content team is the reason I am still here after more than 7 years. For me it is not just a work environment, as there is also a strong community feel across the whole Federation, with many social and well-being events taking place.
Louise, Senior Administrator
I have enjoyed working at Stocklake Park School for many years and find it to be a highly dynamic and stimulating environment. Working in a busy school office, no two days are ever the same and I enjoy rising to new challenges, supporting our staff, students, and parents, and ensuring that the admin team assists in the smooth running of the school. There is a wonderful feeling of community and support for one another, which inspires loyalty and trust. Everyone in the school works together to create a safe, friendly, and nurturing environment for our students to grow and develop, enabling them to achieve their full potential.
Jamie, Facilities & Estates Technician
From the time I sat down in my interview, I was bought in to the new and intriguing vision and saw it as a fresh challenge. I enjoy every aspect of my job, from seeing projects progress and how they benefit the children to it helping me develop skillsets that I wasn’t even aware I had. Every day is different with lots to do but I don’t see it as a job as I genuinely love what I do. What makes it even better is developing bonds with the children and seeing their progression through the schools.

The Vale Federation of Schools is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff, workers and volunteers to share this commitment. The successful candidate will be required to provide two satisfactory references, undertake pre-employment checks including a health check and have a cleared Enhanced Disclosure & Barring check. An online search (including social media checks) will be carried out for all shortlisted candidates as part of our recruitment process

July 2024 – Duke of Edinburgh
Duke of Edinburgh Bronze Award
For a number of years now, Stocklake Park school has been offering the Duke of Edinburgh Bronze Award to its 6th formers. This is an internationally recognised award and involves helping the community/environment, becoming fitter and healthier, developing new skills, planning, training for and completing an expedition. It is offered to the year 13 & 14 students.
We run it on a 2 year cycle with the last cohort of 4 students completing and achieving their award in July 2024, with their expedition being run at College Lake (near Tring) and Stanwick Lakes (Northampton). As always the students exceled and had a great time.
